findings.issue_text: P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `const token = res?.data;` — the sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, which has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and the next access throws instead of refreshing credentials.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(` — the sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so `expiresIn` and `accessToken` are unavailable and the refresh path cannot work.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` — converting a Zod schema to a computed object key creates a literal implementation string rather than matching arbitrary numeric expiry fields, so normal token responses cannot satisfy the intended schema.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — `data: { key },` — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result wrapper rather than parsed credential data, so Prisma receives `{success,data}` instead of the credential key shape.

P1 confidence 100 — apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — `export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) {` — the credential-writing webhook has no HTTP-method acceptance check, so unsupported GET/PUT requests fall through into parsing and can fail as 500s instead of a defined 405 response.

P1 confidence 100 — apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `const reqBody = appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);` — malformed webhook bodies are not handled, leaving the new public endpoint's validation-error path as an uncaught exception rather than a defined 4xx response.

P1 confidence 100 — apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `const keys = JSON.parse(` — invalid ciphertext, a wrong encryption key, or decrypted non-JSON has no handled acceptance behavior and crashes the webhook instead of returning a defined rejection.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {` — the sync path lacks defined handling or fallback for timeout, network failure, and non-2xx responses, so an obvious dependency-failure case is unaddressed across every migrated integration.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — `const state: IntegrationOAuthCallbackState = JSON.parse(req.query.state);` — malformed or structurally invalid OAuth state has no validation/error acceptance behavior, allowing callback requests to terminate with an uncaught parse error.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) {` — the placeholder refresh-token behavior lacks acceptance criteria or verification for providers that omit refresh tokens, leaving whether existing tokens must be preserved unaddressed.

P1 confidence 100 — docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — `Review the change.` — the task defines no acceptance criteria or validation evidence for credential creation/update, shared refresh success, provider failure, malformed payloads, team credentials, or disabled-sync fallback, and the diff adds no tests demonstrating these behaviors.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `const token = res?.data;` — the shared-sync branch returns a native `Response`, not a Gaxios response, so `data` is undefined and every synchronized Google token refresh crashes before updating credentials.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — `data: { key },` — `key` is the entire Zod `SafeParseSuccess` wrapper rather than `key.data`, corrupting the credential JSON shape so later Google credential parsing fails.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` — this computed property creates a required literal `[object Object]` field rather than expressing arbitrary numeric expiry fields, causing normal synchronized token responses to be rejected.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(` — the helper has a heterogeneous contract and returns a native `Response` in sync mode, but this caller treats it as a parsed `HubspotToken`, producing `NaN` expiry and undefined access tokens.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106 — `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token,` — after refreshing and persisting a new Salesforce access token, the connection is still constructed with the stale pre-refresh token, so requests continue failing despite a successful refresh.

P1 confidence 75 — apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — `const appCredential = await prisma.credential.findFirst({` — credential synchronization uses check-then-insert without an atomic upsert or demonstrated uniqueness invariant, so concurrent deliveries can create duplicate credentials and later updates arbitrarily target only one.

P2 confidence 75 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {` — every supported integration synchronously depends on one external endpoint with no timeout, circuit breaker, or fallback, allowing a hung sync service to cascade into hung calendar/video operations across users.

P1 confidence 75 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` — a fabricated refresh-token sentinel is persisted as if it were a real provider token, so disabling sync or routing the credential through a local refresh path later submits invalid credentials and makes recovery impossible.

P1 confidence 100 — apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, an omitted header compares `undefined` to `undefined`, fail-opening authentication and allowing unauthenticated credential overwrite for any user.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:39 — `members: { some: { userId: req.session?.user.id, accepted: true } }` — any accepted team member, rather than an administrator, is authorized to create or replace team-scoped OAuth credentials, enabling privilege escalation across the team.

P1 confidence 75 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — `const state: IntegrationOAuthCallbackState = JSON.parse(req.query.state);` — OAuth state is accepted as unsigned attacker-controlled JSON with no session binding or nonce verification, enabling OAuth login-CSRF or credential planting into a victim user or team context.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `const token = res?.data;` — the shared-sync branch returns a native `Response`, not a Gaxios response, so `data` is undefined and every synchronized Google token refresh crashes before updating credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` returns either the result of `fetch()` (a native `Response` object) when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, or the result of `refreshFunction()`. In `GoogleCalendarService.ts`, the `refreshFunction` returns `fetchTokens.res` which is a Gaxios response with a `.data` property. However, when the credential sync path is taken, `fetch()` returns a native `Response` object which does NOT have a `.data` property - you need to call `.json()` on it. The code then does `const token = res?.data;` which would be `undefined` for the native Response, causing `token.access_token` and `token.expiry_date` to fail. This is a real bug in the credential sharing code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — `data: { key },` — `key` is the entire Zod `SafeParseSuccess` wrapper rather than `key.data`, corrupting the credential JSON shape so later Google credential parsing fails.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the result of schema.safeParse(response), which is a SafeParseReturnType object containing {success: boolean, data?: T, error?: ZodError}. In line 100, the code does `data: { key }` where key is this SafeParseSuccess wrapper object, not key.data. This would store {success: true, data: {...actual credentials...}} instead of just the credential data, corrupting the stored credential format. This is a real bug that would cause credential parsing to fail on subsequent reads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` — this computed property creates a required literal `[object Object]` field rather than expressing arbitrary numeric expiry fields, causing normal synchronized token responses to be rejected.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys. In JavaScript, `z.string().toString()` returns '[object Object]' (the string representation of the Zod schema object), not a dynamic key pattern. This creates a schema that literally requires a property named '[object Object]' with a number value, rather than allowing arbitrary string keys with number values. This is clearly a bug - the developer likely intended to use z.record() or similar to express 'any string key maps to a number', but instead created a broken schema that will reject valid token responses that don't have a literal '[object Object]' property.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for refreshOAuthTokens in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it returns a fetch Response object.
